texts.preamble: A.Vimala vs The Commissioner on 11 March, 2016 Author: T.S. Sivagnanam Bench: T.S. Sivagnanam In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated : 11.03.2016 Coram: The Honourable Mr.Justice T.S. Sivagnanam W.P.No.4691 of 2016 A.Vimala .. Petitioner Vs 1 The Commissioner Corporation of Chennai, Rippon Buildings, Chennai-600 003. 2 The Regional Deputy Commissioner (North) Office of the Regional Deputy Commissioner Corporation of Chennai, No.62, Basin Bridge Road, Old Washermenpet, Chennai-600 021. 3 The Revenue Officer, Revenue Department, Corporation of Chennai, Rippon Building, Chennai-600 003. 4 The Assistant Revenue Officer, Zone Iv Division 36, Corporation of Chennai Old Washermenpet, Chennai-600 021. 5 The City Health Officer, Public Health Department, 6 The Additional Health Officer, A.Vimala vs The Commissioner on 11 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63934748/ 1 Office of the Regional Deputy Commissioner Corporation of Chennai, No.62, Basin Bridge Road, Old Washermenpet, Chennai-600 021. 7 The Assistant Health Officer, Zone Iv Division 36, Corporation of Chennai Old Washermenpet, Chennai-600 021. 8 The Commissioner of Food Safety 5th Floor, Dms Office Building, 359 Anna Salai, Dms Campus, Teynampet, Chennai-600 006. 9 N.S.Chandran Proprietor-Madurai Pandiyan Chettinad Hotel 116/1 Erukkencherry High Road, Sharma Nagar, Chennai-600 039.
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this Writ Petition seeking for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus to direct the respondents 1 to 8 to take action against the 9th respondent, who is running a hotel in the said premises, which has been leased out by the petitioner to the 9th respondent. 4. Several issues have been pointed out by the respondents which include unhygienic atmosphere prevailing in the hotel, change of user of the premises than for the purpose, for which it had been leased out, carrying on cooking adjoining an open drainage canal and various other allegations. 6. Presumably, after notice was ordered in the Writ Petition, the 4th respondent appears to have initiated some action in the matter. Counter affidavit of the 4th respondent states that on receipt of the complaint, the 4th respondent along with the License Inspector, Division - 36, Zone IV conducted an inspection on 21.02.2016 and found that the 9th respondent is using a total extent of 1660 sq.ft contrary to the license obtained by the 9th respondent for 960 sq.ft. and the 4th respondent has given a show cause notice to the 9th respondent to explain the additional usage of area contrary to the license granted to him. 7. The complaint given to the Health Department regarding the unhygenic condition of the hotel was entertained and the complaint has been forwarded to the Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department for necessary action and after receipt of the reply from the 9th respondent to the show cause notice issued and after receipt of the report from the Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner, after reiterating the factual matrix, referred to the representations dated 19.12.2015 received by the 4th respondent on 21.12.2015, wherein, among other things, the petitioner has stated that the trade licence of the 9th respondent should not be renewed, which has been followed by other representations dated 11.01.2016, 14.01.2016, 23.01.2016 and 28.01.2016 and since no action had been taken, the present Writ Petition has been filed. 8. Further, learned counsel for the 9th respondent submitted that there is a landlord-tenant dispute between the petitioner and the 9th respondent and the 9th respondent has filed a suit before this Court in C.S.No.110 of 2016 and an order of interim injunction has been granted in O.A.No.125 of 2016 dated 03.02.2016 by which, the 9th respondent's possession and enjoyment has been protected and it is stated that the suit is still pending and the order of interim injunction is in force.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner, after reiterating the factual matrix, referred to the representations dated 19.12.2015 received by the 4th respondent on 21.12.2015, wherein, among other things, the petitioner has stated that the trade licence of the 9th respondent should not be renewed, which has been followed by other representations dated 11.01.2016, 14.01.2016, 23.01.2016 and 28.01.2016 and since no action had been taken, the present Writ Petition has been filed. 8. Further, learned counsel for the 9th respondent submitted that there is a landlord-tenant dispute between the petitioner and the 9th respondent and the 9th respondent has filed a suit before this Court in C.S.No.110 of 2016 and an order of interim injunction has been granted in O.A.No.125 of 2016 dated 03.02.2016 by which, the 9th respondent's possession and enjoyment has been protected and it is stated that the suit is still pending and the order of interim injunction is in force.
